main_body: A tapered hexagonal coffin lid with a gold cross, tan-orange wood, drawn as one large slab with a dark outline and a darker lower foot section
top_band: none distinct: the coffin is a single lid slab from row ~2 to ~30, orange-brown with a cross. No separate lighter top band over a front face.
evidence: The coffin is drawn as a top-down plan: the whole shape is the lid with a cross seen from above, with a tapered outline. There is no front (south) face under a top band. The lower part (rows 24-30) is a slightly darker foot area with a shaded right strip, but it reads as the continuation of the lid, not a vertical face. This matches the guide's red 'top-down slab (no front)' case.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown, tinted toward the wood, and not pure black, which is in line with the Beodeul approach. The lid has about 4 steps (light tan highlight, orange mid, darker brown, deep brown edge) plus a gold cross with a darker shadow bar. The large lid areas are mostly flat orange with only a few rows of variation and little grain or speckle, whereas the references carry per-plank grain and many more colours per tile. It is cleanly drawn but a bit thinner than the references.
